File surface: the workflow declaring the `Build & E2E` job, and whatever it invokes to install system/browser dependencies — **locate by reading, then declare the real surface in the PR** (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: **no** — this restores a gate to working order; it changes no contract, no accept set, and no published surface. ⛔ Any change that would make the gate *quieter* is out of scope by the card's own terms.
Serial constraints cleared: **PR #5295 (issue #5261) holds `.github/workflows/cross-repo-issue-closer.yml`, `.github/workflows/lint.yml`, root `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml`** — open, awaiting review, surface measured by `git diff --name-only origin/main...`. The `Build & E2E` job is declared elsewhere; if the fix genuinely requires one of those four files, **stop and report** rather than editing across a live hold. Other holds are all package-scoped and disjoint: `packages/plugin-dashboard` (#5264, PR #5300), `packages/cli` (#4924), `apps/console` (PR #5290), `packages/plugin-view` (PR #5294), `packages/plugin-map` (PR #5297), `packages/components` + `packages/types` (PR #5298).

## Why this one is p0

Maintainer ruling, 2026-08-19, verbatim: **「先修 CI,PR 一律等着」**. The `repo:objectui` accept path is stopped behind this card — six PRs are complete, reviewed-ready and deliberately not being flipped. Every additional round of dev output lands in that queue. This is the bottleneck for the entire lane, not one card among many.

## The two things most likely to produce a false green

1. **PR #5292 passed this job in under 2 minutes** in the same window that #5290 and #5294 hung (full detail in the card). Its diff touches only `eslint-rules/**` and `eslint.config.js`. There is evidently a path-filtered short-circuit, and the hang is on the **full** leg. **A green on a short-circuiting diff proves nothing.** Establish which steps actually run on the full leg *before* drawing any conclusion about frequency, cause, or fix.
2. GitHub Actions cannot run locally. Be explicit, per claim, about what is **measured from a real run** versus **reasoned from the YAML**. Do not present the second as the first — #5261's dev handled exactly this distinction well and it is the standard here.

Counter-probe every zero with a known-present neighbouring term, or it is not a reading.

## ⛔ Not acceptable as the fix

Shortening or deleting the E2E leg, skipping the job, `continue-on-error`, raising the timeout so the hang merely fits inside it, or any other change whose effect is that the gate stops reporting. Gate weakening is on the maintainer floor and is the opposite of this card's purpose — the point is to **restore** the signal. Also ⛔ do not add `required_status_checks` to the `main` ruleset; that is a separate gate-strength decision and the maintainer's call.

If the evidence leads you to conclude the honest fix *is* a scope reduction, that is a fork: **stop and report it** (roll-back clause), do not implement it.

## Verification bar

A green `Build & E2E` on a PR that provably takes the **full** leg. Name the path filter and explain why your diff trips it.

## ⭐ Correction: three statements in this card, as I wrote it, are false

The dev measured them. All three were mine, and one of them was the card's headlined warning and shaped its verification bar. Correcting them here because the card is the record.

### 1. "It never reaches the build or the E2E run" — false

The console build **completed** before the hang: `built in 6.69s`, `Console build artifact is ready`. The job gets past the build and dies later, at browser provisioning.

### 2. "The job's total log is ~4.8 KB — it never reaches the build" — false, and the number is not what I thought

`4853` is the log's **line count**, not its byte size. I read a field, assumed a unit, and then reasoned *from* the assumed unit to a conclusion ("this job also produced almost nothing before dying"). A ~4,800-line log is not a job that produced almost nothing. The number never supported the inference I drew from it.

### 3. ⚠️ The path-filter short-circuit theory — **entirely fabricated by me**

The card's most prominent section warned that PR #5292's sub-2-minute pass proved a path-filtered short-circuit, that the hang lived only on the "full leg", and that a green on a short-circuiting diff would be a false green. I put it under a "**do not skip it**" heading and wrote it into the verification bar: *"name the path filter and explain why your diff trips it."*

**There is no such short-circuit.** PR #5292's job log `95987067483` shows it ran the **full E2E suite** (`23 skipped / 10 passed (17.1s)`), and its files (`eslint-rules/**`, `eslint.config.js`) match **none** of the five exclusion pathspecs. Sub-2-minutes is simply what the full leg costs when apt behaves.

I observed a timing difference, invented a mechanism to explain it, never checked whether the mechanism existed, and then promoted the invention to the card's central caution — in the same document where I instructed the dev to counter-probe every zero. I sent it hunting a path filter that does not exist. It found the truth anyway and said so.

## What the fault actually is

`pnpm exec playwright install-deps chromium` — the **cache-hit** step — shells out to `apt-get update` as root, and nothing bounded it. A stalled Ubuntu mirror therefore consumed the entire 30-minute ceiling, leaving the check `cancelled`, i.e. **reporting nothing at all**.

And my "systematic, 2/2" framing was also too strong. The dev found the control that settles it: on PR #5290, the `Live E2E (informational)` job `95986118258` ran **the same `install-deps`, on the same commit, starting in the same minute**, and went green in 3m26s. Same everything, different runner, different outcome — **a per-runner transient the workflow had no defence against**, not a property of the workflow.

That distinction matters for judging the fix: it is correct precisely *because* it does not try to make the mirror reliable. It bounds the exposure instead.

A third occurrence was also recorded — my re-run of #5290 (`95993643751`) hung again with the identical last line. The re-run I authorised was, as it turns out, the wrong call twice over: not just unlikely to help, but re-rolling a runner lottery.

## The fix, and why it does not weaken the gate

Apt comes off the happy path (`playwright install chromium`, no `--with-deps`; browsers come from the `actions/cache` step, measured hitting on the very run that hung). The unconditional `install-deps` is replaced by `scripts/ensure-chromium-ready.sh`, which launches the real bundled Chromium, runs `install-deps` under `timeout -k 15s 240s` **only if that launch fails**, re-probes, and **exits non-zero if no browser can be made to launch**.

Nothing is skipped, there is no `continue-on-error`, the ceiling is not raised, and the E2E suite still decides the check. The one new failure mode is **red with a named reason** instead of cancelled — which is the opposite of the gate-weakening this card forbade. `live-e2e.yml` carried the byte-identical shape under a 40-minute ceiling and is fixed in the same PR, declared and justified.

The ablation is the part worth keeping: removing just the `timeout -k 15s "${DEPS_TIMEOUT}s"` bound turned the regression pin red on the predicted assertion — `expected 600014 to be less than 60000` — and **vitest's own 120s per-test timeout could not interrupt it**, because the wait is synchronous. That is the CI defect's exact shape reproduced locally: `timeout-minutes` could only ever cancel the job, never recover it.

## Verdict

`Build & E2E` on PR #5308: **`completed: success`, 08:32:57 → 08:34:07 — 70 seconds.** Remaining checks still running; not flipped yet.
